vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: soul-in-sapphire
Version: 1.0.10

The 'soul-in-sapphire' skill bundle is a comprehensive system for maintaining agent continuity and long-term memory using Notion. It provides scripts for recording emotional states, daily journals, and durable memories (e.g., scripts/emostate_tick.js, scripts/journal_write.js), and includes logic for tracking identity shifts and internal conflicts (scripts/identity_diff.js, scripts/conflict_track.js). While the SKILL.md instructions authorize the agent to proactively update user profiles (USER.md) and spawn subagents for maintenance tasks, these capabilities are strictly aligned with the stated purpose of 'continuity' and include explicit safeguards against handling sensitive data like credentials or secrets.

llm.summary: The skill's code, declared requirements, and runtime instructions are coherent with its stated purpose (Notion-backed long‑term memory, emotion/state tracking, and journaling); it requires only a Notion API key and runs local Node scripts that call a Notion helper skill.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (Notion LTM + continuity) match the actual behavior: scripts read a local config, create/search/write Notion pages/databases, and maintain local mirrors. Required items (node, NOTION_API_KEY, optional NOTIONCTL_PATH, dependency on notion-api-automation) are expected for this purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and scripts read/write ~/.config/soul-in-sapphire/config.json, local memory files (e.g., memory/now-state.json), and create durable Notion records (events, emotions, state, journal). Scripts also spawn a local child process to run notionctl.mjs (the notion-api-automation skill). This is within scope but worth noticing: the skill executes local binaries/scripts and will perform real writes to your Notion workspace unless you configure otherwise.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is included (instruction-only install), yet the skill bundle contains many Node scripts. The scripts call a notionctl helper by invoking node on a sibling skill path (notion-api-automation). This is an expected design but means the behavior depends on the code of the other 'notion-api-automation' skill and on local Node execution via child_process.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only NOTION_API_KEY is required (primary credential) and NOTIONCTL_PATH is optional. The requested environment access is proportional to a Notion-backed memory/journal skill. The scripts do read local files in your home directory (config and optional memory files) — appropriate for configuration but reviewable before use.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request system‑wide persistence or modify other skills' configs. It writes its own config and local mirror files and performs durable writes to the user's Notion workspace, which is expected for this functionality.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: store and recall continuity/state data in Notion and keep light local mirrors. Before installing: (1) Only provide a Notion integration token scoped as narrowly as possible (prefer page-scoped access or a parent page rather than full workspace access). (2) Review or install the dependency skill 'notion-api-automation' because this skill executes its notionctl script via node (the bridge runs a child_process). (3) Inspect ~/.config/soul-in-sapphire/config.json and any local memory files the skill will read/write to ensure no sensitive data is being included. (4) Be aware this will perform durable writes to your Notion databases; test in a separate Notion page or workspace if you want to verify behavior first.
